newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower, waiting on the Fed.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower, waiting on the Fed.

text.p: French shares closed with losses on Monday, as the market took a cautious view ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting, traders said.
Markets are adjusting to a quarter percent pre-emptive rise in U.S. rates but investors were unwilling to commit themselves until a move is confirmed. French bonds were steady.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 7.85 points or 0.3 percent, at 2,579.28. The CAC-40 futures contract was down eight at 2,580 from Friday's close.
Volume was a light 4.8 billion francs.
Utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux rose 2.32 percent to 574 francs, while holding company Cie de Suez fell 1.11 percent to 277.30.

Rumours of a merger between the two firms gripped the market. "The market is betting on the fact that the merger will take place and that Suez will absorb Lyonnaise des Eaux, which means Suez will have to pay a premium to encourage that merger," a trader said.
The two firms' shares had risen sharply in the morning on reports a merger deal would be drafted in time for a presentation to the Suez board meeting on April 1.
Lensmaker Essilor was flat at 1,500 francs and retailer Promodes slipped 0.21 percent to 1,862, after research consultancy Detroyat added the stocks to its big capitalisations list.
